parts.instructions: Part II contains five completion questions (A1–A5, 2 points each) and four work out questions (B1 4 points, B2 5, B3 3, B4 3; show all necessary steps). In this bank A1–A5 are numbered 1–5 and B1–B4 are numbered 6–9.

All answers were solved independently, every calculation (including the similar questions) was checked with sympy (tools/src_matric/mathematics_2021/verify.py), and the method follows the Eritrean MoE Mathematics textbooks Grades 9–12. questions.stem: If A and B are sets such that A ⊆ B, then which of the following is not true?
explanation_steps: A ⊆ B means every element of A is in B, so A ∩ B = A (A true) and A ∪ B = B (B true).
A ∩ (A ∪ B) = A ∩ B = A (C true; in fact A ∩ (A ∪ B) = A for any sets).
A ∪ (A ∪ B) = A ∪ B = B, which equals A only when A = B. Example: A = {1}, B = {1, 2} gives {1, 2} ≠ {1}. So D is not true. Answer: D.
tips: Test the statements with a small example such as A = {1}, B = {1, 2}.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets is not an empty set?

options.A: {x : 1 < x < 2, x is a natural number}
options.B: {x : x² − 2 = 0, x is a rational number}

explanation_steps: A: there is no natural number strictly between 1 and 2 – empty.
B: x² = 2 gives x = ±√2, which are irrational – empty.
C: x² − 4 = 0 gives x = ±2, which are even, not odd – empty (the paper prints 'x² − 4' without '= 0').
D: 2 is an even prime, so the set is {2} – not empty. Answer: D.
tips: 2 is the only even prime number.

similar_questions.stem: Which set is empty?

options.A: {x : x is a natural number, x < 1}
options.C: {x : x is a prime number less than 3}

explanation_steps: The natural numbers start at 1, so none is less than 1.
{0} and {∅} each have one element. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Six pipes are required to fill a tank in 1 hour and 20 minutes. How long will it take, in minutes, if only 5 pipes of the same type are used?
explanation_steps: The number of pipes and the time vary inversely (the total work, pipes × minutes, is fixed).

questions.stem: A shopkeeper purchased 200 bulbs for Nakfa 10 each. However, 5 bulbs were fused and had to be thrown away. The remaining were sold at Nakfa 12 each. What is the gain or loss in percent?
explanation_steps: Gain = 340 Nakfa; gain % = 340/2000 × 100 = 17 % (a gain). Answer: B.
tips: Profit % is always calculated on the cost price.

questions.stem: The value of the sum 1/(1 + logₐ bc) + 1/(1 + log_(b) ca) + 1/(1 + log_(c) ab) is (a, b, c positive and ≠ 1; log_(b) means logarithm to base b)
questions.stem_tex: The value of the sum $\dfrac{1}{1+\log_{a}bc}+\dfrac{1}{1+\log_{b}ca}+\dfrac{1}{1+\log_{c}ab}$ is
explanation_steps: 1 + logₐ bc = logₐ a + logₐ bc = logₐ (abc). By the change-of-base rule 1/logₐ N = (log a)/(log N), so the first term is log a / log abc.
Likewise the other terms are log b / log abc and log c / log abc (common logs).
Sum = (log a + log b + log c)/log abc = log abc / log abc = 1. Answer: C.
tips: Write every logarithm as a quotient of common logarithms: logₐ N = log N / log a.

similar_questions.stem: Simplify 1/log₂ 30 + 1/log₃ 30 + 1/log₅ 30.

questions.stem: Dehab has a total of Nakfa 590 as currency notes in the denominations of Nakfa 50, Nakfa 20, and Nakfa 10. The ratio of the number of Nakfa 50 and Nakfa 20 notes is 3 : 5. If she has a total of 25 notes, then the denominations (numbers of notes), for Nakfa 50, Nakfa 20, and Nakfa 10 are, respectively?
explanation_steps: Let the numbers of 50-, 20- and 10-Nakfa notes be 3k, 5k and 25 − 8k.
So there are 6 fifty-Nakfa, 10 twenty-Nakfa and 9 ten-Nakfa notes. Check: 300 + 200 + 90 = 590 ✓, 6 + 10 + 9 = 25 ✓, 6 : 10 = 3 : 5 ✓.

The correct triple (6, 10, 9) is not printed. Option B lists 9, 10, 6 – the same numbers in the reverse order (Nakfa 10, 20, 50). No option satisfies the conditions in the stated order: e.g. B gives 9 × 50 + 10 × 20 + 6 × 10 = 710. Keyed B as the intended answer.
tips: Check every option against all three conditions (total value, total notes, ratio).

similar_questions.stem: A purse has 1-, 5- and 10-Nakfa notes, 20 notes in all, worth 88 Nakfa. The numbers of 5- and 10-Nakfa notes are in the ratio 2 : 1. How many 1-Nakfa notes are there?
explanation_steps: Let the 5- and 10-Nakfa notes be 2k and k; then there are 20 − 3k one-Nakfa notes.
So 8 fives, 4 tens and 20 − 12 = 8 ones (40 + 40 + 8 = 88 ✓). Answer: A.

questions.review_flag: Defective: the true answer (6, 10, 9) is not among the options; B (9, 10, 6) is the same triple listed in the reverse order. Keyed B.

questions.stem: Find the equation of a line that has a y-intercept of 4 and is perpendicular to the line joining (2, 3) and (4, 2).
explanation_steps: Slope of the line joining (2, 3) and (4, 2): m₁ = (2 − 3)/(4 − 2) = −1/2.
Perpendicular slope: m = −1/m₁ = 2. With y-intercept 4: y = 2x + 4, i.e. 2x − y + 4 = 0.
This equation is not printed. Option E, 2x − y − 4 = 0 (y = 2x − 4), has the correct slope 2 but y-intercept −4; the other options have slopes 1, 2 (intercept −12), 1/2 and 1/3.
E is the closest option (almost certainly a sign misprint); keyed E.
tips: Perpendicular lines: m₁ · m₂ = −1.
Always check the intercept too: put x = 0.

similar_questions.stem: Find the line with y-intercept −1 perpendicular to the line joining (1, 1) and (3, 5).
explanation_steps: Slope of the joining line = 4/2 = 2, so the perpendicular slope is −1/2.

questions.review_flag: No correct option: the required line is y = 2x + 4 (2x − y + 4 = 0). E (2x − y − 4 = 0) has the right slope but y-intercept −4. Keyed E as the intended answer.

questions.stem: If the sum of the squares of the roots of x² + px − 3 = 0 is 10, then p = ______.
explanation_steps: For roots r and s: r + s = −p and rs = −3.
r² + s² = (r + s)² − 2rs = p² + 6 = 10 → p² = 4 → p = ±2. Answer: D.
tips: r² + s² = (sum)² − 2(product).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true?
questions.stem_tex: Which of the following is not true? (A) If $a<b$, then $a^{2}<b^{2}$. (B) If $a>b>0$, then $\dfrac1a<\dfrac1b$. (C) If $a<b<0$, then $\dfrac1a>\dfrac1b$. (D) $a+\dfrac1a\ge 2$ for $a>0$.

options.A: If a < b, then a² < b².

explanation_steps: A fails for negative numbers: a = −3 < b = 1 but a² = 9 > b² = 1. So A is not true.
B: for positive numbers the larger has the smaller reciprocal – true. C: e.g. a = −2, b = −1: 1/a = −1/2 > 1/b = −1 – true (a, b have the same sign).
D: a + 1/a − 2 = (√a − 1/√a)² ≥ 0 for a > 0 – true. Answer: A.
tips: One counterexample is enough to show a statement is false.

similar_questions.stem: Which statement is always true for real numbers a and b?

options.A: If a > b > 0, then a² > b²
options.B: If a > b, then a² > b²
options.E: If a > b, then ac > bc

explanation_steps: Squaring preserves the order of positive numbers.
B and C fail with negatives, D reverses, E fails for c ≤ 0. Answer: A.

Rebound heights sum to 96/(1 − 4/5) = 480 m, travelled twice: 960 m.
tips: Total = h + 2 × (sum of rebound heights) = h(1 + r)/(1 − r).

questions.stem: Solve the following system of equations: 10/(x + y) + 2/(x − y) = 4 and 15/(x + y) − 5/(x − y) = −2.
questions.stem_tex: Solve the following system of equations. $\begin{cases}\dfrac{10}{x+y}+\dfrac{2}{x-y}=4\\[2mm] \dfrac{15}{x+y}-\dfrac{5}{x-y}=-2\end{cases}$
explanation_steps: Let u = 1/(x + y) and v = 1/(x − y): 10u + 2v = 4 and 15u − 5v = −2.
From the first, v = 2 − 5u. Substitute: 15u − 10 + 25u = −2 → 40u = 8 → u = 1/5, v = 1.
x + y = 5 and x − y = 1 → x = 3, y = 2.
tips: Substitute new variables for the repeated fractions to get a linear system.

explanation_steps: x + y = 6, x − y = 2 → x = 4, y = 2. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Two circles with centers A and B touch each other (internally) at point C. If AC = 8 cm and AB = 3 cm, what is the area, in cm², of the shaded region in the figure?
questions.image_alt: A large circle with a smaller white circle inside it touching at the bottom point C. The region between the two circles is shaded dark. A vertical segment runs from A (upper, centre of the large circle) through B (centre of the small circle) down to C.
explanation_steps: The large circle has centre A and radius AC = 8 cm. A, B and C are collinear, so the small circle has radius BC = AC − AB = 5 cm.
Shaded region = large circle − small circle = π(8²) − π(5²) = 64π − 25π = 39π cm². Answer: B.
tips: For internally touching circles the distance between centres = difference of radii.

questions.stem: In the figure, △ABC and △DBC are isosceles triangles (AB = AC, DB = DC, D inside △ABC, and AD extended meets BC at P). Which of the following is not true?
questions.image_alt: Triangle ABC with A at the top and BC horizontal. D is a point inside the triangle on the vertical segment from A to P, where P is on BC. Segments DB and DC are drawn; triangle DBC is shaded.

options.D: AP is a perpendicular bisector of BC

explanation_steps: △ABD ≅ △ACD by SSS (AB = AC, DB = DC, AD common) – A true. Hence ∠BAD = ∠CAD: AP bisects ∠A.
Then △ABP ≅ △ACP by SAS (AB = AC, ∠BAP = ∠CAP, AP common) – C true; so BP = CP and ∠APB = ∠APC = 90°: AP is the perpendicular bisector of BC – D true.
From A, ∠ADB = ∠ADC, so their supplements ∠BDP = ∠CDP: AP also bisects ∠BDC. The statement 'bisects ∠A but not ∠D' is false. Answer: B.
tips: A and D are both equidistant from B and C, so both lie on the perpendicular bisector of BC.

similar_questions.stem: In isosceles △ABC with AB = AC, P is the midpoint of BC. Which statement is true?
explanation_steps: They are supplementary, so each is 90°: AP ⟂ BC. Answer: A.

questions.stem: In the figure, HM is the altitude to the hypotenuse GK of right triangle △GHK. If GM = 18 and KM = 8, then HM = ______.
questions.image_alt: Right triangle GHK with the right angle at H (bottom-left), K at the top and G at the bottom-right. HM is drawn perpendicular to the hypotenuse KG; KM is labelled b, MG is labelled a and HM is labelled c.
explanation_steps: The altitude to the hypotenuse creates similar triangles: △HMK ~ △GMH, so KM/HM = HM/GM.
HM² = GM × KM = 18 × 8 = 144 → HM = 12. Answer: A.
tips: The altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two segments of the hypotenuse.

questions.stem: Given a parallelogram ABCD, and points P, Q, R, and S are midpoints of the sides of ABCD, then area of PQRS = ______ area of ABCD.
explanation_steps: Draw diagonal AC. In △ABC, PQ joins the midpoints of AB and BC, so the corner triangle PBQ has ¼ of the area of △ABC; similarly for the other three corners.
The four corner triangles together remove ¼(area △ABC + area △ACD) + ¼(area △ABD + area △BCD) = ¼ + ¼ = ½ of ABCD.
So PQRS (a parallelogram) has ½ the area of ABCD. Answer: E.
tips: The midpoint quadrilateral of ANY quadrilateral has half its area.

explanation_steps: ∠AQB = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so BQ² = AB² − AQ² = 64 − 16 = 48.

questions.stem: A1. If the median of 4, 6, x, 9, 10, 19 is 7.5, then x = ______.
explanation_steps: There are 6 values, so the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values in order.
If 6 ≤ x ≤ 9 the ordered list is 4, 6, x, 9, 10, 19 and the median is (x + 9)/2 = 7.5 → x = 6.
Check: 4, 6, 6, 9, 10, 19 → (6 + 9)/2 = 7.5 ✓. (If x < 6 the median would be (6 + 9)/2 = 7.5 as well, so any x ≤ 6 works; x = 6 is the value obtained from the listed order.)
tips: Always order the data before finding the median.

questions.review_flag: Strictly, every x ≤ 6 gives median 7.5 (the 3rd and 4th ordered values are then 6 and 9). The expected answer is x = 6; teachers may accept 'x ≤ 6'.

b) Clearing the denominators correctly (1); x = 7 with the restrictions checked (1).
tips: State the restrictions before clearing denominators.

questions.stem_tex: B2. Let $f(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{x+2}$. a) Find the x- and y-intercepts. b) Find the vertical asymptote. c) Find the horizontal asymptote. d) Sketch the graph.
questions.answer: a) x-intercept (1, 0); y-intercept (0, −1/2). b) x = −2. c) y = 1. d) Hyperbola f(x) = 1 − 3/(x + 2): for x > −2 it rises from −∞ (near x = −2) through (0, −1/2) and (1, 0) towards y = 1; for x < −2 it falls from +∞ (near x = −2) towards y = 1 from above.

subparts.label: d
subparts.question: Sketch
subparts.answer: Two branches in the upper-left and lower-right regions of the asymptotes
steps: Use a table of values on each side of x = −2.

explanation_steps: b) Denominator zero at x = −2 (numerator −3 ≠ 0 there): vertical asymptote x = −2.
c) Numerator and denominator have the same degree: horizontal asymptote y = 1/1 = 1.
d) Division: f(x) = 1 − 3/(x + 2). The graph is the curve y = −3/x shifted 2 left and 1 up; it never meets y = 1.
Table: f(−5) = 2, f(−3) = 4, f(−1) = −2, f(0) = −1/2, f(1) = 0, f(4) = 1/2. The branches lie in the upper-left and lower-right regions formed by the asymptotes.
marking_points: d) asymptotes drawn and both branches in the correct regions through the intercepts (2).
tips: Draw the asymptotes as dashed lines first, then plot a few points on each side of x = −2.

questions.stem: B3. Prove that the measure of the exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the opposite interior angles. That is, prove that m(∠x) = m(∠a) + m(∠c). (3 points)
questions.image_alt: Triangle ABC with A at the bottom-left, B at the bottom-right and C at the top. The interior angles are labelled a at A, b at B and c at C. Side AB is extended beyond B, and the exterior angle between the extension and BC is labelled x.
questions.answer: In △ABC, a + b + c = 180° (angle sum of a triangle) and x + b = 180° (∠x and ∠b form a linear pair). Hence x + b = a + b + c, so x = a + c.
explanation_steps: Given: △ABC with interior angles a (at A), b (at B), c (at C); side AB is extended beyond B, forming the exterior angle x at B. To prove: m(∠x) = m(∠a) + m(∠c).
1. m(∠a) + m(∠b) + m(∠c) = 180° – the sum of the interior angles of a triangle.
2. m(∠x) + m(∠b) = 180° – ∠x and ∠b form a linear pair (A, B and the extension are collinear).
3. m(∠x) + m(∠b) = m(∠a) + m(∠b) + m(∠c) – from 1 and 2 (both equal 180°).
4. m(∠x) = m(∠a) + m(∠c) – subtract m(∠b) from both sides. ∎
marking_points: Angle sum a + b + c = 180° with reason (1).
Linear pair x + b = 180° with reason (1).
tips: A linear pair of angles adds up to 180°.

questions.stem:
B4. Find the variance and standard deviation for the following data. (3 points)
xᵢ: 4 8 11 17 20 24 32
fᵢ: 3 5 9 5 4 3 1
questions.answer: N = 30, mean = 420/30 = 14; Σf(x − x̄)² = 1374; variance σ² = 1374/30 = 45.8; standard deviation σ = √45.8 ≈ 6.77.
explanation_steps: Variance (textbook population formula) σ² = Σf(x − x̄)²/N = 1374/30 = 45.8.
marking_points: σ ≈ 6.77 (1). Accept the sample formula (1374/29 ≈ 47.38, s ≈ 6.88) if used consistently.
tips: Use a working table with the columns x, f, fx, x − x̄, f(x − x̄)².

similar_questions.stem: Find the variance and standard deviation of: x = 2, 4, 6, 8 with f = 1, 2, 2, 1.

questions.review_flag: The textbook uses the population variance (divide by N) → 45.8, σ ≈ 6.77; a sample variance (divide by N − 1) gives ≈ 47.38 and s ≈ 6.88 – teachers may accept either.
